recommended_minimal_set.pattern: value uniqueness under an explicit scope

actual_cases.constraint: unique among Plans in the same direct or top-level Plan container

recommended_minimal_set.semantics: For every resolved selector group, no two selected direct values of p are equal. `WITHIN SELF` means values of one property occurrence; another selector may group sibling instances.
examples: UNIQUE_VALUES Atom/(.Role: Plan).Work Sequence Number WITHIN CONTAINER(Plan)
recommended_minimal_set.ambiguity_to_close: `same direct or top-level Plan container` needs one exact CONTAINER selector definition; decide whether equality is lexical, normalized, or reference identity.

defer_until_a_broader_model_is_defined.why_deferred: These Properties currently use stored strings, registry names, and source references with different resolution times. Define whether a reference stores an ID, a canonical name, or a graph link before adding one format. Existing `[atom id]` and `[scope unit]` formats already cover two literal encodings.

short notation is required when admitted

defer_until_a_broader_model_is_defined.why_deferred: No governing ValueSet or whitelist binding is defined in this packet. Literal `in(...)` is already sufficient for closed sets; a dynamic admission reference without its authority would be an empty predicate.

non_patterns: Claim fence rules and Scope Unit ancestry currently have one Property-specific occurrence each; do not add syntax solely for them.
Do not use transition syntax for static value cardinality, or effective-value syntax to manufacture stored values.

routed_to_operations.syntax_option: A transition context with `PREVIOUS(p)`, `CHANGED(p)`, and `SAME(p)`, e.g. `IF CHANGED(Atom.Content.Summary) THEN CHANGED(Atom.ID)`.
routed_to_operations.why_deferred: It requires a first-class predecessor/successor or rebuild pairing, accepted-edit/no-op event semantics, and a clock definition. Without them, this would confuse static instance invariants with lifecycle rules.
